equities.name: TSX Composite
equities.context: The S&P/TSX Composite closed at 34,938, up 0.8% on the week — the advance ran against a goods-producing GDP backdrop, with mining, quarrying and oil-and-gas extraction GDP down 2.1% m/m in March and the broader extraction aggregate 1.5% lower year-over-year.3 Materials supplied the lift even as crude retreated: copper settled at US$6.51/lb, near its 52-week high of US$6.58/lb and up 35.59% year-over-year, while gold held US$4,353.30/oz, up 31.07% from a year earlier, offsetting an energy sub-index drag as WTI fell 11.74% on the week to US$80.58/bbl.32 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the materials advance to the database's 642 active mining, quarrying and oil-and-gas projects carrying US$263.1B in tracked value, of which 551 active mining projects account for $199.9B.32 If copper holds above US$6/lb and gold above US$4,000/oz, those 551 mining projects would retain the commodity-price coverage cited in their public filings, while the 91 active oil and gas projects ($63.2B) remain exposed to WTI sitting above the $74-76 breakeven cluster the engine tracks.32 Copper's print marks its highest level in the 52-week window, against a one-year average of US$5.24/lb.32

equities.name: S&P 500
equities.context: The S&P 500 closed at 7,466, up 0.5% on the week — the move firmed ahead of the June 16-17 FOMC meeting reflecting the rate-path setup, and Summary of Economic Projections, the first decision under new Chair Kevin Warsh, with market pricing reflecting a hold at the 3.50-3.75% target range.21 The federal funds target has been held since the April 29 FOMC decision, and core CPI ran +2.6% year-over-year on the March reference, the rate backdrop shaping the broad US tape.23 The Philadelphia Fed's Survey of Professional Forecasters recorded Q1 2026 GDP at +2.6%, the data anchor for the week's positioning into the projections release.22

equities.name: Dow Jones
equities.context: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 51,671.03, up 1.10% on the week — the industrial-weighted benchmark advanced as US industrial production for May was released, a read on the manufacturing channel feeding Canadian parts exports, with US unemployment holding at 4.4% in the May Bureau of Labor Statistics print.24 The move tracked rate-path positioning into the June 16-17 FOMC, with the funds target held at 3.50-3.75% since April 29 and the Fed-BoC differential near +125 basis points.21 The 1.10% gain was the firmest weekly move among the major US benchmarks this week, outpacing the S&P 500 and Nasdaq.32

equities.name: NASDAQ
equities.context: The Nasdaq Composite closed at 26,683.94, up 0.3% on the week — the technology-weighted index posted the smallest gain of the four benchmarks ahead of the FOMC projections release on June 17, reflecting the rate-path setup into the meeting.21 The move tracked core CPI at +2.6% year-over-year on the March reference and a funds target held at 3.50-3.75%, the rate setup framing growth-stock valuations into the meeting.23
